clue.text: Freshwater cod's not usually found in this storage facility

indicators.note: what is not usual is out of its normal order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's remark that freshwater cod rarely turns up in a household chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usually' looks like plain commentary on where cod lives, but it is the anagram signal for FRESHWATER CODS.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of bedroom furniture with sliding compartments is a place to keep clothes, a domestic storage unit.

clue.text: Competitive rider always in hospital department? On the contrary

indicators.note: the surface puts always inside the department; read with what follows, the department goes inside instead
this reverses the stated relationship, so the hospital department goes inside the word for always

parts.note: ever means always
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A query about a horse rider who seems to be forever in some hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'in' puts always inside the department; 'On the contrary' tells you to do the opposite and put the department inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rides in eventing, the equestrian competition of dressage, cross-country and jumping, is a competitive horseman or horsewoman.

clue.text: Dismiss taking time to push out second nail

indicators.note: taking in the time letter as a replacement for something already in the word
the incoming letter forces out the letter for second, a replacement

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: A boss dismissing someone after timing them, pushing out a second nail sounds like a carpentry instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... to push out' swaps the S of SACK for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a small, broad-headed nail, as used for carpets or upholstery.

clue.text: Piece tabloid people penned in serious paper

indicators.note: enclosed as if in a pen, so the tabloid and people sit inside the paper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a serious British newspaper
a rag is a disparaging word for a downmarket newspaper
men means people

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about tabloid journalists written up by a heavyweight rival paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned in' means enclosed; the Financial Times, printed on pink paper, is the classic crossword serious paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off part, a synonym of a piece or bit.

clue.text: Allowance taken from Horatio Nelson

indicators.note: the letters are lifted straight out of the run of the admiral's name

explanation.surface: A sailor's daily allowance issued by Admiral Horatio Nelson himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across HoRATIO Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed share or quota allotted to each person, such as a sailor's daily tot.

clue.text: Classroom display showing emblem of Richard III before his end

indicators.note: the emblem comes before the final letter in the answer

parts.note: Richard III's personal badge was a white boar
his refers back to Richard, whose last letter is D

explanation.surface: A history lesson showing the boar badge of Richard III ahead of the king's death at Bosworth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his end' seems to be Richard's death, but it is simply the last letter of Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiteboard is the wipe-clean panel at the front of a classroom on which the teacher writes.

clue.text: Studying in redbrick university

definitions.meaning: poring over books or texts, the act of studying
redbrick describes British universities founded in the late 19th and early 20th centuries

explanation.surface: A student studying at one of the newer English universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading means studying a subject at university, and Reading is also an English university town.

clue.text: See vet providing help for the bat

parts.note: to sight is to see or spot
to screen is to vet or check

explanation.surface: Going to the vet for advice on helping a bat, the flying animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' suggests the animal, but it is a cricket batsman; a sightscreen is the white board behind the bowler that helps the batsman see the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, this large screen beyond the boundary gives the batsman a plain backdrop against which to see the ball.

clue.text: Liking song by writer

indicators.note: next to, so the writer and song sit side by side

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a song composed by a particular writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness or strong inclination for something, so it is a liking.

clue.text: One artist on TV quiz show is Arab

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
QI is a British TV quiz show hosted first by Stephen Fry

explanation.surface: A contestant on a television quiz turns out to be an Arab artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Iraq, an Arab country, is an example of an Arab.

clue.text: Cockney bigamist has this nonsense

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang a wife is 'my old Dutch', so a man with two wives has a pair of them

explanation.surface: A London East Ender with two wives talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is Cockney for wife (from duchess), so a bigamist has two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means gibberish or language that cannot be understood.

clue.text: Foodstuff farm animals finding no good

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: goats are farm animals

explanation.surface: Livestock finding the feed is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain eaten as porridge or fed to horses, a staple food.

clue.text: Finished being entertained by mischievous beggar

indicators.note: a guest is held within the host, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: impish means mischievous
over means finished

explanation.surface: A finished performer being entertained by a naughty beggar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beggar' looks like a noun but is the verb, to make poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar someone is to reduce them to poverty, the same as making them poor.

clue.text: Character of the dump portrayed by French artist — only one small smear

parts.note: Stig is the title character of the children's book Stig of the Dump

indicators.note: one of the two letters for small is all that remains, so one is removed

parts.note: Henri Matisse was a French painter

explanation.surface: A painting of a children's book character by Matisse, smudged with one small smear.
explanation.walkthrough: Stig of the Dump is a classic British children's novel by Clive King.
explanation.definitionFit: To stigmatise someone is to brand or disgrace them, a figurative smear on their name.

clue.text: Male singer with a single exception holds special attraction

indicators.note: one piece contains the other inside it

parts.note: bar one means except for one
it means sex appeal or a special allure

explanation.surface: A male singer, bar one, has a special allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male voice between tenor and bass, or a singer with that voice.

clue.text: I'm surprised US soldiers could be the Queen's companions?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Amazement that American soldiers might be keeping the Queen company.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for keeping Pembroke Welsh dogs of this breed as pets.

clue.text: Me acting outrageously having a certain attraction

indicators.note: behaving wildly, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: An actor boasting that their outrageous performance has star appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic thing draws iron, and a magnetic person is charismatic and compelling.

clue.text: No huge complex is adequate

indicators.note: complicated or tangled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building that is not enormous is still perfectly adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a noun for a building but is an adjective signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sufficient for a purpose is adequate, a synonym of the answer used as an adjective.

clue.text: Oxford University row about learner, one having no connections

indicators.note: around, so the row goes round the learner

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A row at Oxford University about a student who has no contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something isolated and detached from the main body is an outsider standing alone.

clue.text: Drama school endlessly involved in work in USA and part of Canada

indicators.note: taken inside, so the shortened school goes into the word for work

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, work

indicators.note: a word with no ending loses its final letter, so the school's abbreviation is cut short

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: A drama school graduate working in America and Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the drama school to RAD, and 'involved in' places that inside the American spelling of work, which the clue flags with 'in USA'.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland region of the Canadian province Newfoundland and Labrador.

clue.text: Old habit that could make beer better

definitions.meaning: habit in its sense of clothing: a close-fitting man's jacket of the Renaissance
a doubled letter, TT, placed inside the word beer turns it into the word better

explanation.surface: A traditional practice that might improve the quality of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a custom but means garment; a doubled letter is also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a men's close-fitting jacket worn in the 15th to 17th centuries, and also a pair of identical letters.

clue.text: British wildcat seen in spring

parts.note: the ounce is the snow leopard, a wild cat

explanation.surface: A British wildcat spotted in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but means a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap or rebound, which is what a ball does when it hits the ground.

clue.text: Diagnostic technique upset dour sultan

indicators.note: knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy ruler annoyed by a medical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: High-frequency sound waves are used for medical scans, a non-invasive way to examine the body.

clue.text: Block inexperienced reporter heading east

parts.note: a cub is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A junior journalist heading east is stopped by a roadblock.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid with six square faces is a block shape, like a sugar lump or dice.

clue.text: The second person in Shakespeare to get short measure

definitions.meaning: the archaic singular pronoun for you, used in Shakespeare's time
a unit of one thousandth of an inch, a very small length

explanation.surface: An actor playing second fiddle in a Shakespeare play gets short-changed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the old familiar form of you, and also an engineering unit of a thousandth of an inch.

clue.text: With daughter absent, perhaps son and I will deliver hot food

indicators.note: the letter abbreviating daughter is missing

parts.note: a son is an example of a child

explanation.surface: With his daughter away, the son and I will cook up something spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chili con carne, a spicy meat dish, is often just called by the name of the hot pepper.

clue.text: Crazy male will make hard case

parts.note: nuts means crazy
he'll is a contraction of he will

explanation.surface: A deranged man will turn into a tough guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard case' seems to be a tough person, but means a hard outer covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard woody covering of a nut is a protective case.

clue.text: Film wet area in French cheese bar

indicators.note: the wet area goes inside the combined cheese and bar

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
a counter is a bar where drinks are served
a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: A soggy patch of French cheese left on a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the wet area inside the cheese-and-bar pair, exactly at the point where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is a 1945 David Lean film about a romance at a railway station.
